# Small-size font advances

Original controls generated by tools/outline_text_advances_fixture.py. The
package scaffold comes from this project's original Latin ligature controls;
all document text here is independently authored. No font binaries are included.

Twenty-four pages cover Cambria, Arial and Calibri at 10, 11, 12 and 14 pt,
regular and bold. A contrasting END marker exposes the preceding text advance;
two further paragraphs exercise wrapping. The reference application exported the
reference PDF retained in scratch storage. tools/record_outline_text_advances.py
records native positions and hashes without redistributing the PDF or fonts.

Small Cambria bitmap strikes quantize browser advances at 10 and 12 pt. The
independent marker errors reach 7.38 pt. Outline-scale shaping removes these
errors while retaining the original kerning threshold and absolute spacing.
Other tested families/sizes retain essentially the same measured advances.
The reference application positions include accumulated native rounding, so the marker comparison
allows 0.3 pt (the largest unchanged baseline error is 0.248 pt).

Relevant OOXML declarations are Part 1 sections 17.3.2.26 (rFonts), 17.3.2.38
(sz), 17.3.2.19 (kern), and 17.3.2.35 (spacing). This is a browser font-metric
correction, not a demonstrated contradiction of a normative OOXML algorithm.
